elements.element: No minimum purchase commitment imposed on Customer
elements.evidence: "Customer commits to purchase no minimum amount of Services"

elements.element: Fees payable only for usage or ordered Services
elements.evidence: "and pays only for Services ordered or used"

elements.element: Removal of take-or-pay mechanic / absence of penalty for shortfall
elements.evidence: original "on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights" deleted

elements.element: Commitment limited to the current 12-month term
elements.evidence: clause states "no minimum amount ... in each of the next three years"; no 12-month-term commitment exists
no reduction-on-notice mechanic in the redlined text

elements.element: Shortfall settled by true-up rather than penalty

reasons: The locked preferred level is fully satisfied: § 2.1 now imposes no minimum amount and expressly limits fees to Services ordered or used, and the USD 2,000,000 take-or-pay with no reduction or termination right is deleted.
The edit is a targeted in-place replacement of the single offending sentence; it adds no free-standing reduction or termination right, no fallback true-up mechanic, and no boilerplate.
Fallback elements (12-month cap, 30-day reduction notice, true-up) are absent, which is correct — they belong to a separate bargain and are only offered in the non-operative comment.

Intent preserved: § 12.3's no-minimum-volume acknowledgement is untouched and now consistent with § 2.1; the residual phrase "in each of the next three years" is harmless surplus of the original sentence and creates no obligation or dangling mechanic.
